timeline.title: Choose your Grade 12 courses
timeline.description: Check the prerequisites for every program you're interested in and make sure your Grade 12 timetable includes them.

timeline.title: Summer: catch up on a missing course (optional)
timeline.description: If you are missing a prerequisite, summer school, night school, or e-learning through your school board may help. Ask your guidance counsellor.

timeline.title: Application portals open
timeline.description: OUAC (universities) and ontariocolleges.ca (colleges) open for the new application cycle.

timeline.title: University equal consideration date
timeline.description: Applications received by this date get equal consideration at Ontario universities.

timeline.title: College equal consideration date
timeline.description: Applications received by this date get equal consideration at Ontario colleges.

timeline.title: Mid-term marks sent to schools
timeline.description: Your school sends your marks to the programs you applied to. Keep your marks up all year.

timeline.title: Offers of admission
timeline.description: Programs send offers. Check each portal for the date you must respond by.

supplementary.title: CASPer (situational judgment test)
supplementary.what: An online test that shows you everyday situations and asks how you would respond. It looks at things like communication, ethics, and empathy rather than school knowledge.
tips: Book your test date early; seats and dates are limited.
Practise explaining your reasoning, not just your answer.
Check the official site for the current format and fee.

supplementary.title: Video assessment (Kira-style)
supplementary.what: An online assessment where you record short video or written answers to questions within a time limit.
tips: Test your camera, microphone, and internet before you start.
Answer the question asked, clearly and briefly.

supplementary.title: Personal statement
supplementary.what: A short piece of writing about why you want to join the program and what experiences prepared you.
tips: Use real examples from volunteering, jobs, or school.
Answer every prompt the program gives.
Ask a teacher or counsellor to read a draft.

supplementary.title: Interview
supplementary.what: A conversation, in person or online, where the program learns more about you. Some programs use several short interviews in a row.
tips: Learn about the profession and what the job involves.
Practise with a friend, family member, or counsellor.
Have a question or two ready to ask them.

supplementary.title: Information session
supplementary.what: Some programs ask applicants to attend a session that explains the program and its requirements.
tips: Check whether attendance is required and how to register.

readiness.title: Vulnerable sector check
readiness.what: A police background check needed to work with patients and other vulnerable people.
readiness.when: Usually before your first clinical placement.

readiness.title: Immunization records
readiness.what: Proof of vaccinations your program requires. Programs list the exact vaccines.
readiness.when: Usually before your first clinical placement. Some vaccines take several doses over weeks or months, so start early.

readiness.title: Tuberculosis (TB) test
readiness.what: A skin or blood test showing you do not have active tuberculosis.
readiness.when: Usually before your first clinical placement.

readiness.title: N95 mask fit test
readiness.what: A test to find an N95 respirator mask that seals properly on your face.
readiness.when: Usually before your first clinical placement.

readiness.title: CPR / Basic Life Support (BLS)
readiness.what: A certificate showing you can do CPR. Programs often require a specific level, such as BLS for health care providers.
readiness.when: Usually before your first clinical placement. Certificates expire, so check the dates.

costs.label: Tuition
costs.description: Set by each school and program. Listed on each program page when verified.

costs.label: University application fee (OUAC)
costs.description: Paid when you apply through OUAC.

costs.label: College application fee (ontariocolleges.ca)
costs.description: Paid when you apply through ontariocolleges.ca.

costs.label: Supplementary test fees
costs.description: Some programs require tests like CASPer, which charge a fee.

costs.label: Placement readiness costs
costs.description: Police checks, vaccinations, CPR courses, and uniforms can cost money.

costs.label: Licensing exam and registration fees
costs.description: Paid after you graduate. Listed on each profession's page when verified.
